hints: Focus on what filtration actually does here, it keeps solids behind and only lets dissolved ions through into the filtrate.
Recall how Group 2 sulfate solubility changes down the group, with $\text{MgSO}_4$ very soluble and $\text{BaSO}_4$ essentially insoluble.
Ask yourself which sulfates are soluble enough to stay in solution, pass the filter paper, and then crystallise on evaporation.
walkthrough:
**Understand the preparation method**

Think of this as a standard base plus acid preparation. The excess solid is filtered off, and the dissolved product is recovered from the filtrate.

$$\text{QCO}_3(\text{s}) + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{QSO}_4(\text{aq}) + \text{CO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$$

**Spot the key condition for success**

For you to get $\text{QSO}_4$ after evaporation, the $\text{QSO}_4$ formed must be soluble enough to be in the filtrate. If it is insoluble, it will be trapped on the filter paper with the excess $\text{QCO}_3$ and lost.

**Apply the Group 2 sulfate solubility trend**

Solubility of Group 2 sulfates decreases sharply down the group. Magnesium sulfate is very soluble, calcium sulfate is sparingly soluble but enough dissolves, while strontium and barium sulfates are effectively insoluble.

$$\text{MgSO}_4 \text{ soluble} > \text{CaSO}_4 \text{ slightly soluble} > \text{BaSO}_4 \text{ insoluble}$$

**Decide which metals work**

Magnesium works well because its sulfate stays in solution. Calcium just works because enough dissolves to recover a sample. Barium fails because $\text{BaSO}_4$ precipitates immediately and is filtered off, so evaporation of the filtrate gives nothing.

options.A: Incorrect. While calcium and magnesium work, barium does not. $\text{BaSO}_4$ is extremely insoluble, so it would be removed by filtration with the excess $\text{BaCO}_3$ and no product would be in the filtrate.
options.B: Incorrect. This includes barium, which is the trap. Students sometimes confuse sulfate solubility with hydroxide solubility, which increases down the group. For sulfates the trend is opposite, barium sulfate is insoluble.
options.C: Incorrect. Calcium alone is too restrictive. Calcium sulfate is only sparingly soluble, but enough passes through to give a sample, and magnesium sulfate is even more soluble, so magnesium must also be included.
options.D: Correct. $\text{MgSO}_4$ is soluble and $\text{CaSO}_4$ is sufficiently soluble to pass through the filter and be recovered on evaporation. $\text{BaSO}_4$ is insoluble and would be filtered off, so only calcium or magnesium can work.
